newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE leader in jubilant homecoming after surgery.
newsitem.headline: UAE leader in jubilant homecoming after surgery.

text.p: President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan of the United Arab Emirates, 78, returned home to a jubilant welcome on Wednesday after surgery in the United States.

Wearing a medical collar around his neck, he arrived in the UAE capital Abu Dhabi to what al-Khaleej newspaper billed in advance as "a grandiose welcome befitting a noble son of the soil who has worked tirelessly for the welfare of his people and country".

Sheikh Zaid, the Gulf's elder statesman, has been absent since July 1 when he left for private visits to Morocco and Geneva. He underwent surgery on a vertebra in his neck at the Mayo Clinic in Minnesota on September 27 followed by a period of convalescence in Spain and Morocco.

Rulers of the other six emirates in the UAE federation, cabinet ministers and diplomats lined the tarmac after his jumbo jet touched down, state-run television showed in a live broadcast from Abu Dhabi airport.
Senior officials and family members kissed Sheikh Zaid on his nose and forehead, a traditional display of Gulf Arab loyalty, against the sound of a 21-gun salute.
Motorcycle outriders escorted his white Mercedes at the head of a motorcade through crowds lining the route to his palace.
Schoolgirls and women -- all wearing traditional long black dresses and headscarves -- stood on one side of the road. Men in white robes stood on the opposite side.

The UAE capital has had a face-lift in recent weeks, part of nationwide preparations for the homecoming and to mark twin celebrations on December 2 -- the emirates' silver jubilee and Sheikh Zaid's 30 years as ruler of Abu Dhabi.

Thousands of people in the other emirates are due to drive to Abu Dhabi on Friday to take part in a "march of loyalty" at the end of which Sheikh Zaid will receive what organisers believe will be the world's largest bouquet -- 45 square metres (484 square feet) of flowers.
